texts: It is common to use the simple present tense to talk about jobs and occupations as we saw on the useful language before.
I work as a store manager.
What do you do for a living?
The verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED

The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use auxiliaries to make questions and to deny an action. 

Do - I/You/We/They
Does - He/She/ It (3rd person singular)
*Remember pronunciation tip from unit 2.
In the following chart you will see how this structure can be implemented.
Does he work in a bank?
I don’t work as a waiter / Do you work as a waiter?

texts: 1. Most of the verbs take “-s” when using the third person rule.
2. Verbs that finish in “-sh”, “-ch”, “-s”, “-ss”, “-z”, “-x”, “-o”, receive “-es” when using the third person rule.
3. Verbs that finish in “-y” change to “-i” + “es” when using the third person rule.*
*When the “y” is preceded by a vowel letter, just add “s” at the end of the verb.
When talking about Jobs and referring to an individual, we need to use the articles a – an (also called indefinite).
As you can see in the examples, ‘a’ is used before words that start with consonants and “an” before words that start with vowels.

texts: Simple present tense helps us to talk about and describe jobs and occupations. In this chart you will see two main functions covered by this structure when talking about jobs.
We use verb TO BE to state what people are, as in the example provided.
We use other verbs to specify what people do.

They bake cakes.
